name: Scales, modes and melody writing (mode colour, motifs, phrasing)
goal: Choose a scale/mode for the mood (Lydian bright -> Phrygian dark), use the characteristic note, and write motifs with call-and-response and rule-of-three phrasing.

source.note: Written from established production practice to fill a library gap; no single source video.

theory: Modes of the major scale share notes but change the tonal centre; each has a characteristic degree (Lydian #4, Dorian natural 6, Phrygian b2, Mixolydian b7). Pentatonics remove semitones for safe melodies.
prerequisites: DAW or the numpy renderer in sample-lab

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Rendered part or recipe following the workflow

constraints: Portable recipe; not affiliated with any vendor; do not copy factory presets or sample packs.
Numbers in variants come from the source video transcripts; workflow steps are the consolidated mainstream practice.
Bring drums in early and avoid pitch wobble unless asked (user preferences from daily tests).

steps.action: Pick mood -> mode: Lydian dreamy, Ionian happy, Mixolydian bluesy, Dorian cool, Aeolian sad, Phrygian dark.
Emphasise the characteristic note on strong beats over a tonic drone.
Write a 1-2 bar motif using mostly steps with one leap; end phrases on chord tones.
Repeat motif twice, vary the third time (rhythm or ending).
Call and response between two instruments; keep melody in its own register.
For generative melodies lock to scale/pentatonic and limit range.
Hear the theory: run `/home/box/audio-tools/bin/python sample-lab/theory/scales_modes.py` from the repo root and compare the sections; reuse its functions as a starting point for renders.
steps.expect: WAV in sample-lab/theory/out/ demonstrating the principle

verification: Render a short test and A/B against a reference at matched loudness
Run the generator and confirm it writes a WAV without error
Check mono compatibility and that no element masks the kick/bass
